Kai H: FYI the mkdocs build on main started failing after we upgraded the mkdocs-include plugin. The symptom: included README headings get double-hashes in generated anchors (e.g., `#examples` -> `#examples--1`). Kai H: build log snippet: ``` Warning: duplicate anchor generated: examples (examples--1) Linkcheck: /docs/usage#examples -> broken ``` Luis R: include plugin appends suffix if duplicate heading ids are found to avoid collisions. But downstream slugifier in our link resolver normalizes differently between builds. docs-bot: opened issue #478 to track include-plugin dedupe vs slugifier mismatch Maggie L: quick mitigation: convert included README chapters to explicit frontmatter `slug` or dedupe headings in the include. For short term I'll add a build-time postprocessor that collapses `--\d+$` suffixes in anchors when generating the link index. Kai H: can you add a test that ensures link index normalizes `examples--1` -> `examples`? we need parity across local dev and CI. Maggie L: pushing PR 8560 with postprocessor + test. Test uses mocked HTML: `

Examples

` -> slug `examples`. ci-bot: docs/linkcheck (pull/8560) queued ci-bot: docs/linkcheck (pull/8560) failed Kai H: failure shows another case: `examples--` (trailing dash) from headings ending with punctuation removed by slugifier. I'll update regex to strip trailing dash groups and numeric suffixes. Maggie L: updated, retesting. ci-bot: docs/linkcheck (pull/8560) passed ✅ Luis R: leaving a note: this postprocessor is temporary; we should upstream a consistent slugifier in both mkdocs and our docusaurus builds. Followup issue #479. Kai H: thanks, merging PR 8560. Also adding a brief note in CONTRIBUTING: "avoid duplicate headings across included docs; prefer per-page slugs" Maggie L: added that and a small script to find `id=".*--\d+"` in built site for periodic audit.
